text:
Ask "music or quiet?" If they want music, keep it low, and if a track starts pulling the experience somewhere unwanted, change it. This is a bad time to defend the playlist.

Offer water without forcing it, and keep it to sips, since a lot of water fast is dangerous on MDMA. Speak slowly and use fewer words. Please don't explain the universe at somebody who is already frightened by it.
section: Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes
reader: someone looking after a person in a frightening psychedelic or MDMA state, in the first few minutes, once the immediate dangers (keys, stove, roads, more of the substance) are dealt with

sentences.s: If they want music, keep it low, and if a track starts pulling the experience somewhere unwanted, change it.
sentences.payoff: the helper learns to keep music low if the person wants it, and to change a track that pulls the experience somewhere bad
sentences.follows: answers his "music or quiet?" with his "Lower the sound" and his track line in one sentence

sentences.s: This is a bad time to defend the playlist.
Offer water without forcing it, and keep it to sips, since a lot of water fast is dangerous on MDMA.
sentences.payoff: the helper learns to offer water gently and keep it to sips, and why: a lot of water fast is dangerous on MDMA
sentences.follows: after the room and the music, the person themselves: water first

sentences.s: Speak slowly and use fewer words.
Please don't explain the universe at somebody who is already frightened by it.

checked.point: a lot of water fast is dangerous on MDMA
checked.found: MDMA raises antidiuretic hormone while people drink heavily, which can drop blood sodium (hyponatremia), with seizures and brain swelling; the guide's MDMA section and its sodium warnings already rest on this
checked.still_needed: yes: it is why sipping matters, which a fresh reader asked

placement: after the room paragraph: the music next (his paragraph), then water and how to talk (what was left of his fixes paragraph, in his words)

questions.Q2: PASS: the water instruction now says what sipping is for (a fresh reader asked); the music instruction says what to do if they want music
questions.Q3: PASS: exact things: the lights, five concerned people, touch, heat, cold, the bathroom, someone untrusted
questions.Q9: PASS: try 2 trades try 1's packed lists for one act a sentence with the things in the room named (a lamp, another room), and no list of three
questions.Q1: PASS: each sentence says its point first
questions.Q4: PASS: "it" in "keep it low" is the music
questions.Q5: PASS: "If they want music" answers his question; the water paragraph starts a new step, the person rather than the room
questions.Q6: PASS: room, then music, then water and talking: the order a helper works in
questions.Q7: PASS: each is something a helper does in the first minutes

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first; a study after the question it answers)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
